best_for: Students, testers and home users who want free virtual machines on a Windows PC or Intel Mac, and businesses that will check the Extension Pack license before rolling it out.

points.title: The base app is GPL and free
points.text: The main VirtualBox package is open source under GPLv3, and you can run Windows, Linux and other guests on Windows, macOS, Linux and Solaris hosts.

points.title: The Extension Pack is not free for work
points.text: The Extension Pack uses Oracle's PUEL license: free for personal use on one host and for teaching, but commercial use needs a paid Enterprise license. Oracle's FAQ says those licenses start at a minimum order of 100, with a 30-day evaluation available.

points.title: Apple silicon runs Arm guests
points.text: There is a separate download for Apple silicon Macs. Version 7.1 added Arm virtualization for Linux and BSD guests on those Macs, and 7.1.2 removed the beta label from the macOS Arm interface. Plan on Arm guest systems there, not your old x86 VMs.

points.title: Hyper-V can get in the way
points.text: HashiCorp's Vagrant docs, which use VirtualBox as their example provider, warn that VirtualBox VMs can blue-screen Windows while Hyper-V is turned on, and list the commands to switch it off.

points.title: Older versions on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 51 versions as a machine-wide 64-bit installer. macOS lists only the current release, in Intel and Apple silicon builds, so downgrades there need another source. Linux packages come from VirtualBox's own Linux downloads page.
